api/Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Game.GameSess.summary: Class GameSession Namespace Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Game Assembly Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.dll A live game between one human, always South, and three SimpleAiStrategy seats. It is what every Hawsey UI drives: the UI calls the human's moves and the AI-advance methods, and redraws on StateChanged. The AI moves are paced so a person can follow them. public class GameSession Inheritance object GameSession Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Thread safety: the AI loops resume on thread-pool threads after their delays while human moves arrive on the UI thread, so two moves can race for the same turn. So every transition of _state runs under _sync, and each one re-checks, inside the lock, that it is still the right phase and player's turn. A stale human move (a double-tap, a tap during an AI turn) is ignored and reported as false. _generation increments on every new game, so an AI loop that wakes up after New Game stops instead of playing into the new game. Events are raised outside the lock. Constructors GameSession() Initializes a new instance of the GameSession class, with the AI seats paced so a person can follow their moves, and a fresh random deal for each game. public GameSession() Fields HumanPosition The seat the human plays. The AI plays the other three. public const PlayerPosition HumanPosition = South Field Value PlayerPosition Properties Bids Gets the bids made so far in the current round, in bidding order: a snapshot, so a UI can show each seat's bid. Empty before the first bid of each deal. public IReadOnlyList<PlacedBid> Bids { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<PlacedBid> CurrentState Gets the current game state, or null before the first game. public GameState? Returns true if human needs to bid. public Task<bool> AdvanceAiBiddingAsync() Returns Task<bool> AdvanceAiPlaysAsync() Advances AI plays. Returns true if human needs to play. public Task<bool> AdvanceAiPlaysAsync() Returns Task<bool> AdvanceAsync() Plays the AI seats' moves, phase after phase, until the game needs something from outside: a move from the human, or the UI's go-ahead for the next round. This is the loop every UI runs after each human move, so they all drive the game the same way. The human's last card of a round is played here too, since there is no choice to make. public Task<WaitingFor> AdvanceAsync() Returns Task<WaitingFor> What the session is waiting for; Nothing when no game has started, or a newer move (such as a New Game) took over during an AI pause. api/Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Game.WaitingF.summary: Enum WaitingFor Namespace Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Game Assembly Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.dll What a GameSession is waiting for once AdvanceAsync() has played every AI move it can: the move a UI must now ask the human for, or the point where the UI decides what happens next. public enum WaitingFor Fields GameOver = 6 The game is over (Winner). HumanBid = 1 The human bids: PlaceHumanBid(BidAction). HumanCard = 4 The human plays a card: PlayHumanCard(Card). Never asked for the last card of a round, which the session plays itself (there is no choice). HumanHawseyExchange = 3 The human, having bid Hawsey, picks two discards: PerformHumanHawseyExchange(Card[]). HumanTrump = 2 The human, having won the bid, names trump: SelectTrump(Suit?). NextRound = 5 The round is scored (RoundScore); the UI starts the next one with StartNextRound() when it is ready. Nothing = 0 Nothing: no game has started, or a newer move (such as a New Game) took over while this advance was paused. The UI has nothing to show for this call.

api/Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Game.html.summary: Namespace Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Game Classes GameEngine The core game engine that manages state transitions for a Hawsey game. Each method takes the current state and returns a new state. GameOverEventArgs Payload for GameOver. GameSession A live game between one human, always South, and three SimpleAiStrategy seats. It is what every Hawsey UI drives: the UI calls the human's moves and the AI-advance methods, and redraws on StateChanged. The AI moves are paced so a person can follow them. GameState A snapshot of the entire game state at a point in time. Each method on GameEngine returns a freshly-constructed instance rather than mutating the previous state, so callers should treat the exposed Hands and CompletedTricks collections as read-only — mutating them is unsupported and can corrupt subsequent engine transitions. docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started This guide shows how to start a game with Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine. Prerequisites A project targeting a framework that supports netstandard2.0 (for example .NET Framework 4.6.2 or later, or .NET 8 or later) Installation The package has not been published to NuGet yet. Once it is: dotnet add package Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine Until then, clone the repository and reference src/Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine/Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.csproj from your project. Quick Start using Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Game; using Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Players; using Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Rules; var engine = new GameEngine(); var state = engine.StartGame(HouseRules.Default, PlayerPosition.South, new Random()); // state.Phase == GamePhase.Bidding // state.NextToAct is the first player to bid Move the game forward with PlaceBid, SelectTrump, ExchangeHawseyCards (Hawsey rounds only) and PlayCard. Each takes the current GameState and returns the next one. state.GetLegalPlays() returns the cards the player to act may play. To play a complete game, implement IPlayerStrategy and pass it to GameRunner.RunGame: using Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.Strategy; var final = new GameRunner().RunGame(myStrategy, HouseRules.Default, PlayerPosition.South, new Random()); // final.Phase == GamePhase.GameOver Next Steps Explore the API Reference for detailed documentation Read the Introduction for an overview of the engine See examples/Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine.AotSmoke in the GitHub repository for a program that plays complete games Additional Resources GitHub Repository Contributing Guidelines Report an Issue

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine Documentation
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Wolfgang.Hawsey.Engine is the game engine for Hawsey, a four-player team trick-taking card game played with a 48-card pinochle deck. Overview The engine holds the rules and nothing else. It does no I/O and has no UI. A caller starts a game with GameEngine.StartGame, then moves it forward with PlaceBid, SelectTrump, ExchangeHawseyCards and PlayCard. Each call takes the current GameState and returns the next one. GameRunner plays a complete game with an IPlayerStrategy making every decision. Key Features Pinochle deck: Card, Rank, Suit, Deck, with bowers handled by CardRanking Bidding: BidAction (PassBid, NumberBid, HawseyBid), BiddingResult, PlacedBid Trick play: Trick, PlayedCard, FollowSuitValidator, TrickResult House rules: HouseRules (MustBeat, MustTrump, MinimumBid, PointsToWin) and TrumpMode (Suited or AceHigh) Scoring: RoundScore Targets netstandard2.0 and net10.0; trim- and Native AOT-compatible on net10.0 Getting Help Check the Getting Started guide Review the API Reference Visit the GitHub repository Open an issue on GitHub Issues
